textContent.text: Phin linked her new story-ball with her brain and turned it on. This one played an adventure story that took place on Wizzit, a neighboring planet. Phin went into the family room, where her mother was sorting the family's newest story-balls.
"Mother," said Phin, "we should trade something with Wizzit to get food-pods."

textContent.text: Phin went to find XYZ, her information robot. "What are Wizzitens like?" Phin asked. "Are they all greedy and mean?"
XYZ hummed away, its lights flashing. "There are millions of Wizzitens," the robot chirped. "They are all different, just as the people of Beebott are all different."
"Exactly!" Phin cried. "There must be some people on Wizzit who will trade with me so I can get food-pods. How can I find them?"
"You must travel to Wizzit and ask nicely," XYZ chirped.
"Okay. Also, I need something to trade for the food-pods. What does Beebott have that Wizzitens want?" Phin asked.
XYZ hummed. "There are no libraries on Wizzit. Perhaps they would like some of your story-balls?"
Phin looked around her room at the shelves full of story-balls. She could definitely spare some of them for a trade.
She grinned. "Thanks, XYZ. You're the best!"

textContent.text: Phin got in her family's space rocket so XYZ could take her to Wizzit. After they landed, she and XYZ walked around Wizzit City with her tray of story-balls. Everyone looked strange and different, and some people stared at her.
"What if I can't find anyone who wants my story-balls?" Phin asked XYZ.
XYZ flashed. "Just find someone who looks friendly, and hope for the best."
Phin went up to a tall Wizziten and took a deep breath. "Excuse me, sir, would you like to trade—"
"Sorry, I don't have time," the Wizziten said, walking past her.
Phin remembered what everyone said about Wizzitens being mean and greedy. What if they were right?
Just then, a boy pointed at Phin's tray. "Wow, are those story-balls?" he asked. "I've never seen one in real life before." He picked one up and stared at it, grinning widely.
"Um, y-yes. These are my f-f-favorites," Phin stammered.

"Really?" Phin said. "That would be wonderful!"
The boy winked. "I think today might be the start of something great for both of our planets!"
